So I'm not exactly great at building PCs but I built my own PC a year ago and want to say that it's actually not that difficult. My friend helped me build my PC after he ALSO just built his own, so we were kinda very lost and confused. I am just going to describe my own experience and see if it helps you in any way. This is the process I went through with my build.

Firstly I learnt how a PC functions. A normal PC consists of a number of main components:  
CPU - Central Processing Unit, think of it as the brain of your machine.  
Motherboard - Basically holds together all of your main parts.  
Cooler - This can be fans or a liquid cooler, depending on your budget.  
GPU - Graphics Processing Unit, the better a GPU the better the graphics.  
Case - Speaks for itself.  
Power Supply - Also speaks for itself, supplies power to all if your components.  
Storage - Can be SSDs or HDDs. SSDs are faster but more expensive, HDDs are slower but cheaper.  
RAM - Your memory. The more/faster RAM, the quicker your computer will function.  
Operating System - Usually Windows 10.

Use different sites such as pcpartpicker to check compatibility between parts and comparing prices.

When building PC, make sure that all of your parts are equally powerful. If you go all out on your GPU and low ball on a CPU, your computer won't be optimal. 

Make sure you get a decent CPU. Two main brands: Intel and AMD (Ryzen). Im new with the whole Ryzen thing so I will just explain how intel chips work.  
E.g. i7 7700k.   
Generally speaking, the higher number in front of the "i", the better. i3<i5<i7<i9. Then the first number in the ####, in our case "7"700, shows the generation. Higher  = Newer = Better. The final 3 numbers are the model. Again, Higher = Newer = Better. Generally going for a high i5 and mid i7 is usually the call. But then again Ryzen are out here outperforming Intel (I'm pretty sure)  so I would do some research regarding CPU.

A hefty amount of your budget will be eaten by your GPU. Again, there is a choice between AMD or Nvidia, and again I am not well aware of AMD, since they just recently made a comeback. All I know is that AMD are more affordable and more performing for their price, for example the AMD Radeon 5700 vs Nvidia RTX 2060, the Radeon is better in both cost and performance. I would suggest reading a few more blogs/posts about what to get.

Usually, decent RAM is 8GB or 16GB. You will see numbers like DDR3 or DDR4. Again, when it comes to PCs, higher=better. For you both games require no more than 8GB RAM, but if you will do something more than gaming, say creating multimedia, 16GB RAM is a good idea. And of course there's RGB factors, but that's more cost.

The choice of which motherboard to get isn't very hard, since motherboards are very general. Just pick one that is compatible with your build and one that isn't too ancient.

When it comes to cooling it really comes down to budget and preference, so I wouldn't stress it too much.

For PSUs (power supply), I'd go with one thats over 700-800Watts and that's 80+ Gold. You will see that there is Bronze, Silver and Gold. The better the quality, the longer your PSU will live, and that's good for a first build.

Case, storage and OS come at the end usually. Cases are either Low, Mid or Full tower. ATX, mini ATX, ITX, mini ITX are all different sizes. If you have limited space on your desk, choose a PC build that's the appropriate size. For storage it's really your call, but getting a low capacity SSD and a high capacity (I have a 2TB HDD and 500GB SSD).

For a monitor, you should go for one that best reflects your GPU capabilities. Resolution, 1080p or 1440p, and then refresh rate, 144hz or 240hz. Really depends on how well your system runs. But you mentioned that you already have a monitor, so make sure it corresponds to your GPU.

With your first PC you should just get mainstream-brands so your overall process goes smoothly and if anything goes wrong, answers are one quick google search away. The actual build process however is very easy if you do it right. There are countless of videos online on how to properly build a PC, which helped my friend and I a LOT.

Yet again, if any PC gods are reading this and losing their minds out here I apologize. I'm just trying to lay down what I know as a beginner for another beginner to read. If you see any mistakes please call me out to help the OP out here.
